title: Orbital Sentinel
tagline: Was that spacecraft anomaly a broken sensor, a solar storm, a failing bearing, or an attack?
problem: Spacecraft anomalies have look-alike causes. Stale data from a stuck sensor looks like a replay attack, radiation bit-flips look like injected glitches, and a vanished signal could be jamming. Telling them apart is the hard part, and a wrong call is expensive.
role: Solo project. Sole contributor on GitHub.
approach: Treat the spacecraft as a distributed system: ingest a telemetry stream and run a layered detection engine.
Classify each event into one of five outcomes: mechanical failure, environmental upset, sensor malfunction, cyberattack, or nothing.

Separate confusable cases with the right evidence: sequence counters and timestamps for replay, correlation with NASA DONKI space-weather events for glitches, link SNR/BER against frame rate for jamming.
When the evidence does not separate the hypotheses, say so and hand the case to a human instead of guessing.
outcome: A demo-ready platform running on real NASA telemetry, with explainable attribution, AI-written incident reports and a public read-only demo.

metrics.label: Data
metrics.value: Real NASA telemetry and DONKI space-weather events

title: VeriFrame
tagline: Deepfake detection that reports a calibrated probability and the evidence, never a bare verdict.
problem: Detectors degrade hard on generators they were not trained on, so a model with a strong benchmark score can be much weaker on real-world media. A tool that returns one word asks users to trust a black box.
role: Solo project. Sole contributor on GitHub.
approach: Return a calibrated probability with an explicit uncertainty band and a plain-language label, never a FAKE or REAL stamp.
Ship visual evidence with every number: a Grad-CAM heatmap, a per-frame timeline and a frequency-spectrum plot.
Keep one detection core behind three surfaces: a web app, a Chrome extension and a REST API.
Keep the band table in one file read by both the TypeScript and Python sides so thresholds cannot drift between API and UI.
outcome: A single detection core exposed as a web app, Chrome extension and REST API, with CI and an MIT license.

title: PORTCULLIS
tagline: A prompt-injection detection gateway for LLM apps. Think WAF, but the payloads are natural language.
problem: LLM applications are exposed to adversarial prompts that target the model's instruction hierarchy, and most teams have no equivalent of a web application firewall in front of the model.
role: Solo project. Sole contributor on GitHub.
approach: Put a real-time gateway in front of the model that scores each request through a layered cascade: rule matching, a nearest-known-attack (kNN) sidecar and score fusion.
Expose three dashboard surfaces: live traffic, a decision inspector showing matched rules and per-layer fusion arithmetic, and a red-team console.
Evaluate against a roughly 20k-row test set through the deployed cascade and publish the unflattering findings alongside the headline table.
outcome: All 11 milestones complete, with an eval report that is candid about its limits: the regex-only baseline matches the full learned system at low false-positive rate, and full-cascade latency is over budget.

title: ATTESTA
tagline: An autonomous SOC where every verdict is reproducible and re-adjudicable.
problem: Agentic SOC products let a language model read telemetry and write a verdict, so re-running the process after a model upgrade or new data gives a different answer. The audit trail is a transcript, not a proof.
role: Solo project. Sole contributor on GitHub.
approach: Split reasoning from deciding: an LLM only proposes typed, evidence-cited claims.
A pure Adjudication Kernel turns the admitted claims into a verdict under a versioned policy, so the same inputs give byte-identical output.
Content-address the evidence and pin it to epochs so a verdict can be re-derived months later.
Re-adjudicate old cases against new threat intelligence without re-running inference (Retro-Verdict Drift Detection).
outcome: Pre-release: built in gated phases where each phase has tests designed to fail if it is incomplete.

title: NetSentinel
tagline: An explainable network digital twin for threat detection and attack reconstruction.
problem: Alert-centric tools say that something fired, but rarely why, what evidence supports it, or how activity evolved over time.
role: Solo project. Sole contributor on GitHub.
approach: Turn network telemetry into per-device behavioural baselines and transparent risk scores that list their contributing factors.
Correlate detections into attack chains mapped to MITRE ATT&CK, keeping rule hits, behavioural anomalies, ML anomalies and incidents distinct.
Consume telemetry from existing engines (Zeek, Suricata, PCAP, NetFlow, syslog) rather than replacing them.
Offer a no-login detection playground with generated scenarios and tunable thresholds.
outcome: An MCA research project with a public playground where visitors can tune detectors and see what is flagged and why.

title: Overrank
tagline: A live house-competition platform for campuses with a leaderboard that reacts in real time.
problem: Campus house and team competitions are tracked in spreadsheets, so nobody can watch the standings move or trust how points were awarded.
role: Solo project. Sole contributor on GitHub.
approach: Make the leaderboard, team pages, player profiles and events public and read-only so students never need to sign in.
Restrict sign-in to faculty, who award points, run events and manage the roster.
Keep an append-only points ledger: mistakes are fixed with a compensating entry, never by rewriting history.
Enforce access in the database with Supabase Postgres row-level security.
outcome: Live in production with CI, a scroll-driven 3D landing page, and a season replay view.

title: gitVisualise
tagline: Paste a GitHub link, get an interactive, narrated architecture tour of the repo.
problem: Onboarding onto a codebase means reading a hundred files to learn what talks to what. Hand-drawn architecture diagrams go stale.
role: Creator and main author (85 of 104 commits on GitHub).
approach: Analyse a repository and generate an animated, click-through map of how it works, entirely in the browser with no server or API keys.
Ship the same engine as a website, a CLI, an agent skill and a GitHub Action.
Keep it dependency-free and open for contributions with good-first-issue labels.
outcome: A zero-dependency open-source tool with four surfaces and a public demo on GitHub Pages.

title: AlgoVerse
tagline: A DSA visualisation and interview-prep platform with a real step-through debugger for every algorithm.
problem: Most DSA visualisers either look dated or bury the learning under gimmicks, and every topic ends up with its own one-off animation code.
role: Solo project. Sole contributor on GitHub.
approach: Drive every visualisation from one reusable step-sequence engine with play, pause, step, scrub and speed controls.
Use a consistent visual language where colour always means something (active pointer, visited, found).
Add Supabase-backed gamification: XP, badges, streaks, solved-problem tracking and a leaderboard.
outcome: A live app covering 25 data-structure modules, 13 pattern guides and 635+ explained LeetCode solutions.

title: GLYPHFORGE
tagline: A GPU-native ASCII art engine that matches glyph shapes instead of using a brightness ramp.
problem: Nearly every image-to-ASCII converter indexes a fixed character ramp by tile brightness, so the output reads as scratchy noise rather than a picture.
role: Solo project. Sole contributor on GitHub.
approach: Choose each character by structure-correlated glyph matching, not brightness lookup.
Do colour work in linear light and cluster colours perceptually in Oklab.
Render the whole grid with a GPU-instanced renderer in a single draw call.
outcome: A live browser demo whose output is real, selectable text that preserves hard edges and fine texture.
